headline: US orders diplomats to depart Saudi Arabia amid escalating Houthi attacks, regional conflict
summary: The US State Department has ordered non-emergency staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia due to increased Houthi hostilities, including deadly attacks on civilian targets. This follows an escalation in the Yemen conflict, impacting regional stability.
details: The US State Department has ordered some non-emergency diplomats and their family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia. This decision comes amidst a surge in attacks by Iran-aligned Houthis on civilian targets within the country.

The order follows recent deadly incidents, including an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam that killed one person and injured eight others. Earlier, two people were killed after a drone attack on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield was intercepted.

State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott stated that the Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, targeting critical infrastructure and causing civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions.

This latest withdrawal of diplomatic personnel is a response to an escalation of fighting in Yemen, opening another front in the wider regional conflict. The conflict has been triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran and has impacted global energy trade and Gulf economies.

Washington had previously returned some diplomatic staff to the region after they were pulled out when Tehran launched attacks on US facilities. The US embassy in Riyadh also issued a security alert warning of possible further Houthi attacks.
Four US officials also indicated that US missions in other Gulf states might also order family members to leave, highlighting the broader regional instability.

headline_marked: Sajek road [[blockade resumes indefinitely]], tourists urged to leave as demands remain unmet
headline: Sajek road blockade resumes indefinitely, tourists urged to leave as demands remain unmet
summary: The Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee and Sajek Karbari Association have reinstated their indefinite road blockade after their three-point demands, including the withdrawal of armed JSS members, were not fulfilled.
details: Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee and Sajek Karbari Association have announced an indefinite road blockade on the Sajek tourist road, effective from today. This action comes as their three-point demands, including the withdrawal of armed JSS members, remain unmet by the administration.

The decision was jointly announced yesterday afternoon by Natun Joy Chakma, president of Sajek Karbari Association, and Babudhan Chakma, convener of Sajek Gano Odhikar Rakkha Committee. They stated that the blockade will continue until further notice.
Tourists currently visiting Sajek were requested to leave the area by yesterday, anticipating the disruption. The blockade is expected to significantly impact tourism in the popular hill destination.
Bijoy Kanti Chakma, member secretary of Sajek Gano Odhikar Rakkha Committee, confirmed that the blockade, previously suspended for Durga Puja, would resume. It was enforced from 6:00 AM today.

The organizations had initiated an indefinite blockade on October 11, which was briefly suspended after assurances from the administration. However, as demands were not met within the promised timeframe, the blockade was re-enforced on October 15, and now again indefinitely.
